item.research_question: How does the addition of molybdenum (Mo) in small amounts (1–3 wt %) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of (CoCrFeNi)100−xMox high-entropy alloys in chloride and acidic environments?
item.material_system: (CoCrFeNi)100−xMox with x = 1, 2, and 3 wt % (designated Mo1, Mo2, Mo3)
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting using elements with >99.9 wt % purity, melted at least five times in a WK-∏ furnace; ingots (Φ 35 × 10 mm) annealed for 3 h at 500 °C and air-cooled
item.test_conditions: Microhardness (500 g load, 10 s); compressive tests (Φ 3 × 6 mm, strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹); electrochemical tests in 3.5% NaCl and 0.5 M H2SO4 at room temperature; potentiodynamic polarization scan rate 1 mV/s from −0.5 V to 1.1 V vs. SCE
key_findings: All alloys exhibit a single FCC solid solution, except Mo3 which contains a Cr- and Mo-rich σ phase in interdendrites.
Hardness increases from 124.8 HV (Mo1) to 133.6 HV (Mo3) as Mo content rises from 1 to 3 wt %.
Compressive yield strength increases from 113.6 MPa (Mo1) to 141.1 MPa (Mo3) without fracture under ~60% strain.
In 3.5% NaCl, Mo3 shows a corrosion current density (icorr) of 6.6 μA/cm², an order of magnitude higher than Mo1 (0.4 μA/cm²) and Mo2 (0.24 μA/cm²).
In 0.5 M H2SO4, icorr decreases with Mo content: 34.1 μA/cm² (Mo1), 28.0 μA/cm² (Mo2), and 15.4 μA/cm² (Mo3).
Pitting corrosion in NaCl occurs preferentially at dendrite/interdendrite junctions where σ phase forms.
In H2SO4, Mo promotes formation of Mo(VI) oxyhydroxide or molybdate, reducing dissolution rates in active zones.
item.mechanism: The σ phase formed at 3 wt % Mo causes galvanic corrosion in NaCl due to compositional segregation (Cr/Mo-rich interdendrites vs. Co/Fe-rich dendrites), lowering corrosion resistance. In acidic media, increased Mo content enhances passivation film formation and generates protective Mo(VI) species that inhibit dissolution.
item.limitations: The presence of the σ phase at 3 wt % Mo is described as 'catastrophic' for corrosion resistance in chloride environments; the study only covers as-cast and annealed conditions without thermomechanical processing.
item.future_work: The authors suggest further development of HEA systems that balance strength and corrosion resistance by optimizing Mo content below the threshold for σ phase formation.
quotes: The (CoCrFeNi)97Mo3 alloy exhibits an ordered sigma (σ) phase enriched in Cr and Mo.
The icorr value of the Mo3 alloy is an order of magnitude higher than the other two.
the effect of Mo was to form Mo (VI) oxyhydroxide or molybdate (MoO42−), decreasing the rate of dissolution in active zones.
